1 173(1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (in short "MV Act") for setting aside the impugned order dated 04.08.2009 passed by the Additional Member, MACT, Jaora, District Ratlam in claim case No.54/2008, whereby an award of compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- has been awarded in favour of the respondent No.1 / claimant.
03. The relevant and necessary facts are that on 02.07.2001 when the respondent No.1 / claimant - Ashok Sharma was going on motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-09-LM-8244 driven by one Deependra.

At that time respondent No.2, driver of the offending vehicle i.e. a tanker bearing registration No.MP-14-B-6645 which was being driven by him rashly and negligently, dashed the appellant due to which claimant and Deependra Singh both of them sustained grievous injuries and Deependra Singh died during the treatment and the respondent No.1 suffered permanent disablement from the injuries.
Respondent No.3 is the owner of the said tanker which has been insured with the appellant / Insurance Company.

04. Before the trial Court respondent Nos.2 & 4 remained ex-parte whereas appellant denied all the allegations by submitting that at the time of incident, respondent No.2 was not having any valid and effective license.
The motorcycle driver and its Insurance Company are the necessary party.
Deceased Deependra Singh was not having any valid license, therefore, Insurance Company is not liable for any compensation.

05. Learned Tribunal after framing the issues took both the parties to adduce the evidence and after scrutinizing the evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- in favour of the respondent No.1 / claimant.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellant / Insurance Company has preferred this miscellaneous appeal.

06. Learned counsel for the appellant / Insurance Company submits that learned Tribunal has not Tribunal has erred in allowing the excess compensation to the respondent No.1 which by no stretch of imagination actual bill produced by the respondent No.1 has been allowed to the extent of Rs.1,52,645/-.

Advance paid by the respondent No.1 has also been taken into account, the Tribunal has erred in allowing Rs.71,184/- in the head of pain and suffering which cannot be considered justified in any manner.
The respondent No.1 was Teacher and there is no evidence on record that he was terminated from service as such award of Rs.3,22,000/- for the future loss of earning capacity is highly excessive.
Hence, the impugned award be set aside or reduced.

07. No one appeared on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4.
08.
Learned counsel for the appellant heard at length and perused the entire record of trial Court.

09. The first contention of the appellant is that respondent No.1 / claimant was not having any valid license at the time of accident but from perusal of the record of the trial Court fit appears that the appellant did not examine any witness in support of his contention.

Therefore, on the basis of the statement of respondent No.1/ claimant - Ashok Sharma and other witnesses claimant / respondent Nos.1 to 4 have succeeded to prove their case that at the time of accident the respondent No.2 has driven the offending vehicle but there is no evidence available on record that the respondent Nos.2 The New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Ashok Sharma & Ors.

2 & 3 i.e. driver and owner of the vehicle have violated any terms and conditions of the insurance policy, therefore, the respondent No.1 / claimant's motorcycle was involved in the accident and the respondent No.1 himself sustained grievous injuries.

The respondent No.1 / claimant has proofs,
paper and bills of his treatment Exhibit P/1 to Exhibit P/319 and Exhibit P/313.
10.
On the basis of the aforesaid evidence, it is proved that the expenses for the treatment of respondent No.1 / claimants was Rs.3,17,908/-.

From the perusal of the evidence available on record and various exhibits of claimant's sports career, it is proved that the claimant Ashok Sharma was the player of Volleyball and other games and due to permanent disablement which has been caused in the aforesaid accident, his sports career was spoiled and he was withheld from getting any job on the basis of the sports quota, therefore, trial Court has rightly considered future prospects and loss of future earning.

The respondent No.1 / claimant remained hospitalized for a long period hence, looking to the young age of 25 years of the claimant, his sports career and factum of his permanent disablement, the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the amount of compensation in various heads which cannot be considered as excessive.

11. In view of the above, this Court has no agitation in holding that the findings given by the below Tribunal is just, proper and adequate in respect of the compensation amount, therefore, there is no need for any interference.
12. With the aforesaid observation, this Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed.
No order as to cost.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Divyansh The New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Ashok Sharma & Ors.
